learningGoals: Understand basic addition by combining two groups of vegetables. 🍅
Learn how to 'add on' to a number to find the total sum. ➕
Count objects accurately to find out how many there are in all. 🚜
Use math vocabulary like 'altogether', 'total', and 'more' in daily conversations. 🗣️
teachingTips: Use real vegetables from your kitchen to physically show addition, like 2 tomatoes plus 3 potatoes. 🥔🍅
Encourage your child to count out loud and touch each object as they count to build focus. ☝️
Frequently use the word 'altogether' in simple questions, like 'How many carrots do we have altogether?' 🥕
Praise their effort and keep the learning playful so math feels like a fun farm adventure! 🎉

funActivities.title: Kitchen Farm Addition 🧑‍🍳
funActivities.description: Place a few onions and potatoes on the table. Ask your child to count the onions, then the potatoes, and finally count them all to find the total! 🧅🥔

funActivities.title: Vegetable Drawing Game 🖍️
funActivities.description: Draw 3 carrots on a piece of paper. Ask your child to draw 2 more. Then, let them count the total number of carrots and write the number! 🥕✍️

funActivities.title: Supermarket Counting Mission 🛒
funActivities.description: While shopping, ask your child to put 4 apples in the basket, then add 2 more. Ask them, 'How many apples do we have altogether?' 🍎
